q: Idaho's Snake River Valley AVA keeps its nights cold chiefly because of:
opts: Marine air drawn inland through the Cascades
Deep glacial lakes holding the summer's heat
Fog rolling up the valley from the Pacific
exp: Approved in 2007 as Idaho's first AVA, Snake River Valley reaches west across the state line into Malheur County, Oregon, and its vineyards sit on the bed of ancient Lake Idaho at around 43.5°N. Nothing maritime reaches this far inland — height alone delivers the diurnal swing, with warm days and nights that drop 30–40°F, which is why the wines keep acid at desert latitudes. The real constraint is not summer heat but winter cold and spring frost, so sites are chosen above the valley floor where cold air drains away. Idaho's second AVA, Lewis-Clark Valley (2016), likewise straddles a state line, into Washington.

q: The Douro's vineyard classification letters run from A to F based on a points system measuring what?
ans: Vineyard quality factors (altitude, aspect, schist…) setting the beneficio — each parcel's Port-production entitlement
exp: The cadastro dates to 1947; A-grade vineyards earn the largest Port authorization.

q: Name the three Douro subzones from west to east.
accept: baixo corgo cima corgo douro superior
ans: Baixo Corgo → Cima Corgo → Douro Superior
exp: Cima Corgo holds the quintas of legend (Pinhão); Superior is hottest and newest.

q: Barca Velha, Portugal's first great dry Douro red (1952), was created at which house?
exp: Released only in exceptional years; ~20 vintages in 70 years.

q: Vinho Verde's premium subregion for varietal Alvarinho is:
exp: Higher ripeness, no spritz pretense — Soalheiro and Anselmo Mendes lead.
Burgundian texture on granite; Quinta dos Roques the reference.

q: Bairrada's sparkling and red identity rests on which high-acid, high-tannin grape?
exp: Luís Pato's 'Baga Friends' made it a cause; clay soils, Atlantic air.

q: Colares' pre-phylloxera fame comes from Ramisco vines grown in:
ans: Ungrafted coastal sand dunes (chão de areia)
exp: The louse cannot cross deep sand; tiny production west of Lisbon.

q: Alentejo has a DOC protecting a Roman-era practice of fermenting and macerating in large clay vessels sealed with olive oil. Name the DOC and the vessels.
ans: DOC Vinho de Talha — fermentation and skin maceration in clay talhas (amphorae), traditionally sealed with olive oil; Roman continuity
exp: Granite-country José de Sousa (José Maria da Fonseca) kept it industrial-scale.

q: Moscatel de Setúbal must be at least what percentage Muscat of Alexandria?
exp: ≥85%; Bacalhôa's Moscatel Roxo variant is the collector's twist.

accept: aged in warm lofts without estufa
ans: Slow aging in sun-warmed lofts (no artificial estufagem) — the fine-wine route
exp: Estufagem tanks heat bulk wine to ~45–50°C for three months.

q: Match Madeira noble grape to its style.
exp: Tinta Negra does the volume; 'Rainwater' is a lighter blended style.

q: Which island DOC revived Verdelho-based whites from ungrafted vines in volcanic currais (stone corrals)?
exp: Azores Wine Company led the revival; salt is the terroir.

q: Name Portugal's DOC hierarchy from top to bottom.
accept: denominacao de origem controlada vinho regional vinho de mesa
exp: Many top producers bottle as Vinho Regional to escape blend rules — as in Bairrada.

q: Which Portuguese region covers roughly a third of the country, is known for Touriga Nacional and Aragonez blends on the plains, and is the world's cork capital?
exp: A third of global cork production comes from these plains. Note the Alentejano VR footprint is far larger than the Alentejo DOC, which is eight discrete subregions.

q: What is 'Vinho Verde's' typical alcohol range and why?
ans: ~8.5–11.5% — early picking in a cool, wet Atlantic climate
exp: Alvarinho bottlings from Monção reach 12.5–13% and change the category's meaning.
